page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.medium is an entry-tier, memory-skewed virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 architecture. Operating under the KVM hypervisor, it is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core via hyperthreading, accompanied by 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a high 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware-level features include 35 MB of shared L3 cache alongside instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES.

Benchmark assessments show performance constrained by the single physical core allocation. In synthetic processing metrics, the server records a stress-ng single-core score of 1,102.08 and multi-core score of 2,162.17, with Geekbench yielding 981.0 in single-core and 1,743.0 in multi-core evaluation. Memory subsystem tests demonstrate uncached read bandwidth of 17.2 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 14.52 GB/sec. In application-focused metrics, it sustains 2.52 million operations per second in Redis SET tasks and 2.49 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

The ecs.e3.medium does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external network block storage for persistence. While compute density is low, the provision of 16.0 GB of memory prevents out-of-memory bottlenecks in memory-heavy tasks. This creates favorable resource efficiency for operational profiles requiring significant working memory relative to computational power, such as lightweight in-memory caches, small staging databases, batch queue consumers, and background monitoring utilities.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.medium is a dual-vCPU virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture, powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz and 16.0 GB of system memory. Hosted on the KVM hypervisor, it provides 2 vCPUs running on 1 physical core with hyperthreading, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Architectural extensions include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES. Synthetic testing demonstrates conservative compute throughput, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 1,743.0, a PassMark CPU score of 2,616.1, and uncached read memory bandwidth of 17.2 GB/sec. The instance includes no local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. With its resource allocation heavily emphasizing RAM capacity over CPU execution speed, the ecs.e3.medium is well matched for memory-dependent, low-intensity tasks including small Redis caches, staging database deployments, queuing workers, and internal administrative tooling.
